items.title: Brainfood Live On Air: New Series, How AI Is Changing My Job as a Software Engineer
items.guest_line: Andrew Lawson · Engineering Director @ Monzo; Josh (surname inconsistent in transcript) · Fractional CTO; Simon Hammond · data science background, joining Azuna
items.vendor_flag: No vendor behind a product. Show sponsor Greenhouse gets a read at 3:24 (AI voice interviewer); not part of the discussion.
items.reader_fit: Moderate: a UK in-house or agency tech recruiter gets a practical view of how the engineering role and its junior pipeline are changing, but the content is opinion from three engineers, with few figures.

points.claim: Unspecified design choices become coin flips the agent re-flips each time, so strong engineers state opinions on the choices that matter
points.quote: anything you don't specify, you're asking the agent to flip the coin for you

points.claim: Engineers who understand impact beyond syntax get more from AI, which is a screening signal
points.quote: that person can excel with AI in a way that those who were kind of just knowing the syntax aren't

points.claim: Letting everyone submit auto-generated code swamped the engineering gatekeepers in one consulted organisation
points.quote: the whole rest of the organization drowned them in submissions and ideas and contributions

points.claim: Junior engineering vacancies are said to have fallen sharply, unsourced
points.evidence: Host Hung Lee: 10 to 20% decline, no source given
points.quote: People are talking about 10 15% 20% decline of vacancy.

points.claim: Raise expectations of AI-fluent juniors instead of giving them boring tasks
points.quote: change the expectations that we have of junior engineers and actually expect much more of them

items.title: Brainfood Live On Air: The Next Generation of Background Screening
items.guest_line: Ben Mones · Founder and CEO @ Fama
items.vendor_flag: YES. Guest is CEO of Fama and is launching Fama Lens (GA 15 Nov). All outcome figures (98% review time, 14% to 1.5% decisional rate, $450,000 saved) are his own claims about unnamed customers.
items.reader_fit: Moderate: practical questions to ask a screening vendor and a view on package mix, but examples and law cited are US (FCRA); only GDPR is mentioned for Europe and nothing UK-specific beyond a cannabis aside.

points.claim: Lens is onboarded through a 75 minute policy workshop and a human-corrected policy agent, taking two to four weeks
points.quote: a 75minute policy workshop

points.claim: Vendor claims on Lens outcomes
points.evidence: Mones: 98% reduction in review time, decisional rates 14% to 1.5%, one customer saved $450,000 on labour (vendor claim, unnamed customer)
points.quote: 98% reduction in review time. Average decisional rates dropped from 14 to one and a half percent.

points.claim: Employer policies are often deliberately vague, so discovery questions are needed
points.quote: a lot of companies policies are like very intentionally general, very intentionally vague

points.claim: Agent log revealed the rum recipe behind an apparent false positive on an alcohol-free brand policy
points.quote: In the freaking recipe for the ice cream cake was rum.

points.claim: Ask AI product vendors how much human involvement sits behind it
points.evidence: Mones; Lens line at 50 to 60% gross margin
points.quote: ask about the level of human co-pilot that's associated with it

points.claim: Hung's informal poll of how teams run checks
points.evidence: About 100 votes: 39% point solution, a quarter no checks, 13% ATS
points.quote: Point solution. We have 39%.

points.claim: Would not look at candidates' private AI chats
points.quote: as far as like looking at what they're saying to AI, hell no.

items.title: Brainfood Live On Air: How to Use Claude for Talent Acquisition
items.guest_line: Adriano Herdman (host also says Adriana) · Co-founder @ Move; Alla Pavlov · hands-on recruiter and AI trainer, Amsterdam
items.vendor_flag: Partly. Herdman co-founded Move and promotes his own 24-skill plugin pack (email-gated, 10:40 to 21:05). Greenhouse sponsor read at 38:18. Both guests are Claude advocates who train or sell AI enablement.
items.reader_fit: High: a UK recruiter can copy the intake calibration play, the skill-building steps and the Exa sourcing connector setup today, with GDPR caution flagged by Pavlov.

points.claim: Intake calibration play: transcript plus spec through Clay gives six profiles across three tiers
points.evidence: Herdman: time to alignment from 24 hours to 10 minutes (self-reported)
points.quote: pull together six profiles across three tiers in 2 minutes

points.claim: Time to alignment fell with the skill
points.quote: can be 10 minutes. It used to be 24 hours.

points.claim: Skill design rule
points.quote: one important thing one skill one job

points.claim: Build a skill by recording a repetitive task
points.quote: Claude building the skill out of it and test it

points.claim: Exa free tier covers modest sourcing volume
points.evidence: Pavlov: about 50 to 100 profiles a day on the free plan
points.quote: free plan is enough to source maybe let's say up to 50 100 profiles a day

points.claim: Always tell candidates how you found them
points.quote: always mention how did you find the profiles

points.claim: Teach agents what good recruiters know beyond obvious profile matches
points.quote: they work with another 10 people in that business that haven't updated their profile ever

points.claim: Adoption survey: most at ad hoc or experimenting
points.evidence: Herdman self-reported LinkedIn survey, 162 in-house respondents
points.quote: 89% were at level one or two

points.claim: Live poll on wanted Claude use
points.quote: about 40% of people who voted saying sourcing is number one

items.title: Talent Engineering Hard Truths
items.guest_line: Dan McCarthy · Senior Talent Engineer @ Zapier
items.vendor_flag: No product praised. Zapier is an automation vendor but McCarthy pitches none of its products.
items.reader_fit: High for TA ops and leaders: build-versus-buy rules and pre-build checks apply to UK teams; speaker is US-based and pay comments are not UK-specific.

points.claim: The key skill is knowing what not to build
points.quote: it's about building, but it's also about knowing when to tell you what not to build.

points.claim: Do not rebuild enterprise tools
points.quote: I'm not going to rebuild enterprise software because I'm not going to build it better.

points.claim: Maintenance burden is the reason to buy
points.quote: most software engineers at most companies are not building new features, they're maintaining current ones

points.claim: Reinvest saved time in candidates: 90 minutes versus 30 before offer
points.evidence: McCarthy, stated as a goal not a result
points.quote: now instead of spending 30 minutes before offer, I get to spend 90 minutes with every candidate before offer.

points.claim: Local-only builds cannot be used by others
points.quote: works on your computer but guess what no one else can use it

points.claim: Engineers moving into talent engineering take lower pay
points.quote: I don't get paid the way a software engineer gets paid.
